# SKILL-IMPACT — changes to these skills, and what the runs after them showed

Mode: autonomous          # autonomous = memory.remember applies skill edits itself, in their own
                          # commit; approve = it writes SKILL.md.proposed and you accept with mv

One line per change, newest first. A change is *trialed* on the runs that follow (their worklog
entries carry `Skills: <skill>@<sha>`); `checkup seats` compares `Run:` numbers before/after.
Reverted and rejected changes are logged too, so they are not re-proposed. Outcomes: `proposed` · `trialing` · `kept` · `reverted` · `rejected` · `superseded` (a later change replaced it before its trial could be judged on its own).

| 2026-10-08 | workflow | Four execute rules in `references/phase-3-execute.md`. (1) A deviation that changes a number or assumption a plan Finding rests on (worker count, call rate, limit) stops the run so the Finding and every target derived from it are re-derived before an operator ticket spends money; a one-item probe never proves full-run runtime or cost. (2) Re-grounding after a reset or compaction reads the Execution state and the active ticket, re-opens skill files only when their rules are gone, and opens only the memory pages the ticket names. (3) The freshness stop ends on the closing card with `workflow plan SLUG` as the next action and the drifted files on one line. (4) `Try it: none` says nothing changes on screen and names the test or receipt that shows the change. | retro of a work run (a serializing lock voided the runtime estimate and the paid full run missed its target; repeated whole-file re-reads after compaction; two relayed freshness stops; a user unsure what to test) | 3 runs | trialing |
| 2026-10-07 | workflow | Two closing-card rules and a check. (1) `check-run.py` warns when it runs in a linked worktree or off the primary branch (origin/HEAD, else main/master), naming the primary checkout; the closing card requires the run's commits on the primary branch and pushed first, or asks. (2) The card's `Reads:` names run files and receipts only, never `AGENTS.md` or its kin, which every CLI already loads. Tested 2026-10-07: 2 warnings in the stale worktree of the source run, 0 new warnings on the primary checkout. | 2026-10-03 | workflow · understand | Three small changes. (1) Brainstorm *Restate first*: round 1 opens with **Problem, as I read it**, 2–3 plain lines before any finding; pasted threads compressed, the human's cause/fix guesses kept out and checked as claims. (2) Review: escape hatches (`any`, casts, non-null assertions, suppressed checks, a workaround repeated at unrelated sites, an always-set optional field) are design evidence, P2 naming the design flaw (P1 if a behaviour breaks; boundary parsing exempt); a third mechanical check greps the diff for added hatches (pattern tested: 8/8 planted hits, 0/5 lookalikes, `.workflow/` excluded). (3) understand reads PR body and review discussion via `gh` for the commits behind cited code, cites a PR by merge-commit `data-sha` with `href` to the PR, marks discussion-only reasons as stated intent, and traces history past the latest commit. Also §3a: look for a headless browser before calling a web measurement impossible. Tested (1) on a toy repo with a pasted Slack thread: restatement first, the thread's regex-lib guess checked and refuted, the font remark set aside; the same run asked permission for a browser timing it could have run, hence the §3a line. Judge: round-1 misreads caught by the restatement, P2 design findings later fixed, and explainers whose Decisions cite a PR | pstack `architect` red flags, `principle-type-system-discipline`, `why` (cursor/plugins, MIT); poteto, "Complete Guide to pstack" pt. 2 | 3 runs / 3 explainers | trialing |
